title: a Tensor is three fields
summary: Before the behaviour: the object. Three slots, no array, no shape.

claims.text: Tensor inherits RandMixin, not a base class with storage. The frontend is assembled from mixins; the data model is not in any of them.
__slots__ names exactly three attributes: uop, is_param, grad. There is nowhere on a Tensor to put an element.

__slots__ also removes the instance __dict__. A Tensor is three pointers. tinygrad creates one Python object per graph node, so this is the difference between a graph that fits in memory and one that does not.

The docstring says "multi-dimensional matrix containing elements of a single data type". No field holds elements. Either they live behind uop, or they do not exist yet — and the second case is the design.

beats.text: This is a Tensor. Before we watch what it does, look at what it is. One class line, one docstring, and one line of slots. That is the whole object.
beats.direction: hold on the class line, do not scroll yet

beats.text: uop, is_param, grad. No shape, no strides, no data pointer. If you came from PyTorch you are looking for the array right now, and it is not here.
beats.direction: underline each name with the cursor as you say it

beats.text: Slots is not a micro-optimisation. It removes the instance dictionary. A Tensor is three pointers. This compiler makes one Python object for every node in the graph, so a hundred thousand nodes means a hundred thousand of these — and with a dict each, that is a different program.
The docstring calls it a multi-dimensional matrix containing elements. Read the fields again. The elements are behind uop, or they do not exist yet. That second case is the entire design.
So if the Tensor is not the data, where is the data? Next lesson, we follow the constructor to the only thing it can produce.
